features.feature_value: Kept posts if they lacked slurs and were not viewed as threatening, even if hateful
features.evidence_span: "none of them used slurs" ... "I wouldn't necessarily say any of them were threatening"
features.rationale: Participant ties keep/remove to whether content includes slurs and whether it is threatening.

features.feature_value: Removed mainly posts seen as having no purpose beyond spreading hatred; if either side had merit, they should not be deleted
features.evidence_span: "only ones that had no other point to exist than spread hatred" ... "If both or at least one side had a point it had merit to not be deleted."
features.rationale: Their justification centers on perceived lack of merit/purpose and hatred-only content.

features.feature_value: Would remove if a post states opinion as fact or calls for violence
features.evidence_span: "If one of the posts was stating opinion as fact or calling out to violence I would remove."
features.rationale: They specify a concrete threshold involving violence and misleading presentation.

features.feature_value: Did not evaluate as a pair; banned both when both had name-calling/curse words
features.evidence_span: "I didn't evaluate it as a pair" ... "name calling and curse words. I banned both"
features.rationale: They explicitly report a non-pairwise process and a shared content trigger for removal.

features.feature_value: Inflammatory language served as the deal breaker; alternate perspectives were otherwise acceptable
features.evidence_span: "considered inflammatory language as the deal breaker" ... "Otherwise seeing alternate perspectives was acceptable."
features.rationale: They contrast sensitivity to inflammatory language with openness to alternate perspectives.

features.feature_value: Hardest cases were when one mirror version was much more antagonistic than the other
features.evidence_span: "in some cases, one version was significantly more antagonistic than the other" ... "hardest time with."
features.rationale: Their pair reasoning depends on asymmetry in tone/antagonism across versions.
